claim: Motor-language action-sentence compatibility effect (ACE) did not replicate in an 18-lab preregistered study: N=1,278, effect on log lift-off about 0 [-0.006, 0.004], versus 155-170 ms (about 9%) in the originals. Two 2025 papers (JEP:LMC series; Frontiers third-person study) report no robust effect or only conditional one-directional effects.
agent_test: Not applicable: motor effect in humans; no agent test.

claim: Sentence-picture verification effects for implied shape and orientation are small but present; implied shape replicated (57 and 70 ms, BF01 about 0.01), orientation was weak (33 and 38 ms, d about .10, BF01 0.5 to 1.1), colour flipped sign (157 ms match advantage vs -138/-154 originals).
agent_test: Compare an agent given a text-only description vs one asked to list implied visual states first on shape-dependent questions, equal tokens.

claim: Replication effect sizes in simulation tasks are about half the originals (d .15 to .18 vs .31 for shape), so original studies were inflated.
agent_test: None needed; use as a prior when weighing any simulation-based scaffold gain.

claim: Conceptual-metaphor priming (cleanliness and moral judgment) is weak: original d=-0.60 (N=40) vs direct replication d=-0.01 (N=208); a moderator (response effort) is post hoc.
agent_test: Do not build metaphor priming into the schema; test only if cheap: metaphor-framed vs plain prompt on judgement items.

claim: Facial-feedback (a bodily-state-to-cognition effect) failed to replicate in the 17-lab RRR (pooled about 0.03 on a 10-point scale vs 0.82 original); multi-lab and meta-analytic evidence is mixed. Numbers were not opened. Verified in full: RRR 17 labs, N=1,894, difference 0.03 [-0.11, 0.16] vs 0.82 original. Many Smiles (N=3,878): mimicry and voluntary action tasks work, pen-in-mouth inconclusive (abstract only). Coles 2019: 286 effects, 138 studies, small and heterogeneous (bias-corrected d not found).
agent_test: None.

claim: A three-level meta-analysis finds a small pooled embodied effect in verb processing and learning (g=0.259, 33 samples, 265 effects, N=12,357), but it pools paradigms and is mostly Chinese L2 work.
agent_test: None.

claim: Text-only language models recover perceptual structure: colour-term geometry aligns with CIELAB (RSA tau up to .33 in ELECTRA, only 18 terms), and static embeddings also align, so text statistics carry it.
agent_test: Check whether a scaffold step asking the agent to state sensory properties from text raises accuracy on perceptual commonsense items.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: GPT-4 predicts human sensory similarity judgments well: pitch r=.92, loudness .89 (GPT-3.5), colours .89, consonants .57, taste .54, timbre .42; human split-half pitch .90, consonants .46. Colour naming ARI English 0.59 (corrected from 0.54).
agent_test: Use as a ceiling check: agent ratings vs human norms on held-out sensory items.

claim: LLM ratings track human norms better for non-sensorimotor than sensorimotor dimensions (GPT-4 U=65, P=.018, rrb=.69 in the published version); gap smaller for visually associated dimensions.
agent_test: Probe agent on motor/gustatory concept ratings vs abstract ones; expect weaker on motor.

claim: Vision training is not shown to cause the gain: Marjieh et al. argue gains come from richer text, Xu et al. link gain to visual association; models differ in much more than images.
agent_test: None; model-level confound cannot be tested on one agent.

claim: LLMs fall short of humans on grounded abstract concept properties: no model above r=.37 vs human ceiling >.9 (Chlapanis 2026), though rating alignment is r about .6-.8.
agent_test: On abstract concepts, test whether asking the agent to generate concrete situations (O-step) improves definition-matching vs plain.

claim: Vision-language models show a deficit on affordance descriptions (beta=0.171, CI [0.04,0.30], p=.022) that resists prompting; training captions skew affective.
agent_test: Not testable on a text agent; background.

claim: Visual grounding helps LMs unevenly: Visual+Word models lose to text-only on verb datasets, GIT-style fusion is nearly identical to text-only; multimodal models answer concrete-prompt QA better (68.0 to 77.5%) but confounded by training mix.
agent_test: None.

claim: LM hidden states encode world state: after splicing, T5 generations match the new state 75-87% of time vs 24-38% for single contexts (toy domains). Othello-GPT activation edits cut legal-move error from 2.68 to 0.12 (natural) and 2.59 to 0.06 (unnatural); Gurnee and Tegmark probes for space and time but admit probes do not show use. No causal test on perceptual concepts yet.
agent_test: Ask agent to keep an explicit state table in Alchemy-style tasks vs none, equal tokens.

claim: Blind people share much of sighted knowledge but not all: size ordering 49.7% vs 80.7% agreement, shape odd-one-out 55.1% vs 74.4%; text statistics explain colour less for blind (.21) than sighted (.60) groups.
agent_test: None; argues language carries part but not all of perceptual knowledge.

claim: Theoretical positions: grounding is needed (Bisk 2020; Merrill 2021 formal limits) vs text suffices partly (Mahowald 2024; Louwerse 2011); neither side is decided by present data.
agent_test: None.

claim: Prompting LLMs with conceptual metaphor structure improves outputs in small-model evaluations, but the study is weak (LLM judge, no stats).
agent_test: Replicate with human or fixed rubric on held-out tasks at equal tokens before use.

claim: Embodied-concept theory gives no direct, tested scaffold mechanism for a text-only agent; relevance is background only.
agent_test: None.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Having a text-only LLM write out a state trace per step (Visualization-of-Thought) beats zero-shot CoT on spatial tasks with GPT-4: tiling 63.94 vs 54.15, next-step 55.28 vs 48.61, route success 14.72 vs 9.48; natural-language navigation 59.00 vs 54.00 only p<0.16. Token cost not matched.
agent_test: On spatial or state-tracking items, compare a per-step written state table vs plain CoT at equal output tokens, with a human-checked state-accuracy metric.

claim: Where simulation helps LLM physical reasoning, the gain comes from an external simulator (Mind's Eye: +27.9 zero-shot, +46.0 few-shot points on 39 tasks) or from perspective filtering for weaker models (SimToM, +14.2 to +47 points over CoT, none for GPT-4), not from sensory imagery prompts. No study found tests imagery prompting at equal tokens.
agent_test: Equal-token test of external code or simulator step vs imagery prompt on physics word problems.

claim: Grounding helps text models at fixed scale for embodied and visual-attribute concepts, but modestly and unevenly: CLIP/BLIP beat OPT-175B on mass-type concepts (OPT near chance on mass, 85% on material); multimodal encoders beat BERT on ViComTe; scale did not help ViComTe; PIQA human-model gap 20 points in 2019.
agent_test: None; background.

claim: Blind-versus-sighted evidence points to compensation by language: blind speakers' colour-adjective associations are predicted by text embeddings, and early blind participants rely more on semantic neighbourhood density (N=42, group F(1,39)=9.40). Petilli 2024 not located.
agent_test: None; background.
